title: A Wreck for the Horizon
premise: Desert ranger Noor Joubert chases a thief, Sef, who stole the one thing Noor ever inherited: his late father's brass compass. The chase leads to a tide-revealed sea cave, where Noor discovers the compass is a key to the River Qadash, whose forbidden source is said to grant belonging to whoever drinks first. Sef, it turns out, is the estranged son of the man who mapped the river and erased his own name from its records. Together, rival and thief, they race a seasonal flood upstream, forced to decide whether to claim the source for themselves or reveal the truth: the river belongs to no one, and the villages downstream are already dying of its diversion. In the end Noor chooses truth over inheritance, opening the source to all and losing the compass — but gaining, at last, a place among the people he saved.
about_author: Wendell Sterling is a former surveyor who spent a decade mapping dry riverbeds across three continents before turning to fiction. He writes adventure novels about landscapes that keep secrets and the people stubborn enough to ask them questions.

chapters.title: The Weight of Moving
chapters.summary: POV Noor. On the salt flats, ranger Noor Joubert picks up the trail of Sef, a thief who stole his dead father's brass compass. Flashbacks reveal Noor's rootless life — reassigned every season, belonging to no town. The emotional beat is restless grief: he chases not the object but the last piece of his father, and stopping means feeling it.

chapters.title: What the Tide Gives Back
chapters.summary: POV Noor. The trail ends at a coastline where the retreating tide exposes a sea cave etched with river maps no ranger has ever seen. Inside, Noor is ambushed by Sef — and by strangers who call the cave a tollgate to the River Qadash. Beat: awe curdling into dread as Noor realizes the compass fits a lock here perfectly.

chapters.title: The Tollgate Keeper
chapters.summary: POV Noor. The cave's keeper, an old woman named Ilsa, explains the legend: the river's source grants belonging to whoever reaches it first. She recognizes the compass as the property of Amal Joubert — the cartographer who mapped the river and vanished. Beat: Noor's inheritance transforms from keepsake to obligation, and Sef escapes deeper into the cave system.

chapters.title: Two Thieves
chapters.summary: POV Sef. For the first time we ride with the thief: Sef is the unacknowledged son of Amal Joubert, raised on rumors of a father who chose a river over a family. He stole the compass to claim a birthright he was never given. Beat: bitter symmetry — two sons of one absent man, both chasing the same inheritance, neither willing to share it.

chapters.title: Upstream
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Forced into uneasy alliance when the cave floods behind them, Noor and Sef begin the ascent along the Qadash through canyon country. They trade barbs and, reluctantly, stories. Noor notices the river runs strangely thin. Beat: grudging respect forming, undercut by Noor's dawning suspicion that the river is being bled dry upstream.

chapters.title: The Diverted Village
chapters.summary: POV Noor. In a dying riverside town, the pair finds evidence of an engineered diversion — and learns Ilsa's tollgate is no legend but a business: the source is sold to the highest bidder. Sef's map knowledge proves his father's, deepening Noor's suspicion that his own father was complicit. Beat: loyalty to Amal's memory cracking against accumulating truth.

chapters.title: The Buyer's Men
chapters.summary: POV Sef. Mercenaries hired by the diversion's buyer ambush the travelers to seize the compass — the only working key to the source gate. Sef takes a wound covering Noor, an act he can't explain even to himself. Beat: loyalty vs. truth inverted — Sef protects the brother he resents, and the race becomes a flight with a countdown: the seasonal flood is coming.

chapters.title: Amal's Last Page
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Sheltering in a cartographer's cache, they find Amal Joubert's final journal: he discovered the diversion, tried to expose it, was erased from records and history — the compass was meant for both sons, split between them. Beat: grief and fury fused; the inheritance was never a prize but a duty, and time has nearly run out.

chapters.title: The Source
chapters.summary: POV Noor and Sef, alternating. At the flood's edge they reach the source gate; the mercenaries arrive behind them. In the climax, Noor uses the compass to open the gate but refuses to claim the water, instead breaking the diversion mechanism as Sef holds the mercenaries at the narrows. Beat: the choice between inheritance and truth made at last — at the cost of the compass itself, lost to the flood.

chapters.title: Belonging
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Weeks later, the river runs full again and the diverted villages revive; Noor, compassless, is offered — and accepts — a permanent post in the town he helped save. Sef departs upstream to restore their father's name to the maps, brothers now in truth if not in law. Beat: quiet resolution — Noor finally stops moving, because staying no longer costs more.
